business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil law for private law matters within Quebec; Common law for public and federal law matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part X.2; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1; Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2235-2247; Regulation respecting the disclosure of beneficial ownership information under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, RRQ c. L-44.1, as amended

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of certificate of incorporation or corporate register extract of corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via competent authority in origin (e.g., Global Affairs Canada for federal documents or provincial competent authority for provincial documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed in favor of Quebec formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or authorized commissioning officer in the partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the origin state is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential or business address for all UBOs and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or authorized certifying officer in the relevant jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states) on the notarial certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of police clearance or criminal record extract for all UBOs and general partner managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police records authority or financial intelligence unit of the country of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, accompanied by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing for a foreign corporate general partner (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registrar in the jurisdiction of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via competent authority, with certified French translation if issued in non-French official language

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the US OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and domestic Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; PEP identification in accordance with FATF Recommendations 12 and 22, covered under the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC's interpretive guidance; enhanced due diligence is applied to high-risk jurisdictions, complex ownership structures, and any transaction involving a senior foreign official or domestic PEP threshold of CAD 25,000.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises du Québec (REQ) and the online 'Centre de validation des noms'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11, s. 63) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1, s. 13), an enterprise's registered name must be in French, with a French phonetic transliteration for Latin characters; a non-French name may be accepted only where it is a recognized trademark or corresponds to a personal name, and all accents and grammatical forms must conform to standard Quebec usage; the REQ database will reject names that are primarily English without an authorized exception.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receiving a rejection notice from the REQ, the requester may submit a written administrative appeal to the Registraire des entreprises, including mandatory grounds, a revised proposed name, and any supporting trademark registration or evidence of French language conformity; if the Registrar dismisses the appeal, the requester may apply to the Cour du Québec for judicial review under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 12-24, within 30 days of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with limitations; a registered office and service address in Quebec is required under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, with a physical location necessary solely for registered service; for a low-risk vertical SaaS company, a virtual office staffed by a registered agent and with a service agreement and acceptance of court mail is accepted, provided no banking or securities licensing triggers a physical work-site requirement; the general partner must maintain a real address for inspection in Quebec if it exercises management powers.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections is low at 5% annual probability for this low-risk software vertical; the likelihood increases to 15% if there is a foreign-resident general partner, unusual UBO complexity, or a triggering event such as an AML renewal review or banking inquiry; inspection probability is uniform across all registrants under the REQ's compliance campaign framework.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation fee (validity 90 days)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff under the Quebec tariff of fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Declaration of registration (inscription) filing for limited partnership
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff for enterprise registration; market benchmark for a standard limited partnership declaration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/legalization of corporate records, powers of attorney, passport copies, and police clearances
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in origin jurisdiction and competent authority for apostille or consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff per document and per-document government apostille fee (CAD 30-100 depending on federal/provincial issuer)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of apostilled and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator (member of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per 100 words (approximately CAD $0.15 per word) for an estimated 1,200 words

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing and AML/CFT desktop due diligence - PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External corporate counsel or AML/CFT compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate (2.5 hours at USD $260/hour) plus database subscription pass-through

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and commercial substance setup retainer (first year, pre-paid)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent or corporate services provider in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for annual virtual office service with service of mail and acceptance of court process

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Courier, secure file transfer, and administrative document management
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: International courier service (e.g., FedEx, DHL, Purolator) and secure electronic vault provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for tracked international courier to and from Quebec and digital data room access for one quarter

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), Book IV, articles 2236-2267 (société en commandite) and articles 2186-2229 (partnership generally); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), in particular sections 9-43 on the declaration of registration, name distinctiveness, and filing deadlines; if the general partner is a Quebec corporation, also the Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), operated under Revenu Québec; filings made through the OneStop Business Registry online portal (entreprisesquebec.gouv.qc.ca).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration - Limited Partnership); base state filing fee CAD 84 (approx. USD 62, indexed annually).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership (art. 2236 C.C.Q.). The declaration of registration must state the cash and in-kind contributions made and the balance, if any, promised by each partner (ss. 24-25 L.P.L.E.). No escrow account or deposit is required; partner capital may be funded progressively according to the subscription schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation, acting as general partner of the proposed Quebec limited partnership (the 'Partnership'), approves the Limited Partnership Agreement, including the subscription schedule and capital contributions of the limited partners. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Partnership adopt its registered office at the address set out in the declaration of registration in the Province of Quebec, and that the declaration of registration be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] Secretary, with authority to open bank accounts, engage counsel and accountants, execute the partnership agreement, and complete all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (name search and reservation service, OneStop portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a string search in the Central Register of Enterprises to confirm that the proposed French-language name (mandatory in fact for the Quebec declaration) is distinctive, lawful, and not confusingly similar to existing legal persons, partnerships, or trademarks. File an optional 90-day name reservation and obtain the reservation certificate before submitting the declaration of registration.
required_dossiers: Proposed name strings (at least one in French)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for lack of distinctiveness, re-file with a modified name, attach written consents from prior users, or apply for administrative review within 30 days under section 13 of the L.P.L.E.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement and capital subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Lawyers and notaries in the Province of Quebec; no government filing at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the contrat de société en commandite governed by articles 2236-2267 C.C.Q., identifying the corporate general partner (commandité) and the limited partners (commanditaires), their respective contributions, profit and loss allocation, management powers reserved exclusively to the general partner, transfer restrictions, and dissolution events. The contract is evidenced in writing and each limited partner executes the subscription schedule.
required_dossiers: Capital subscription schedule and contribution records
Certificate of incumbency of the corporate general partner
Notarized or certified copies of partners' identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Civil-law correction: amend the contract by supplementary agreement and re-execute before the declaration is submitted so that the registered particulars match the contract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec via the OneStop Business Registry electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic Déclaration d'immatriculation for a société en commandite, inserting the registered office address in Quebec, the general partner's corporate identity and registered office, the name and domicile of each limited partner, and the amount of paid and promised capital per partner. Pay the CAD 84 fee, and upon validation the Registraire issues the enterprise number (NEQ) and the attestation of registration.
required_dossiers: Copy of the limited partnership agreement
Proof of registration of the corporate general partner
Electronic identifiers of the declarant officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the pre-alerted inconsistencies within the portal and resubmit; if the declarant misses the statutory 60-day deadline (s. 21 L.P.L.E.), pay the applicable late fees and file an amended declaration; request administrative review under section 55 L.P.L.E. for any refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance installation and first board proceedings of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Corporate Secretary; board of directors of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting of the corporate general partner; adopt the pro-forma first board resolution approving the LP agreement, the registered office address, and the appointment of officers; issue share certificates or partnership interest positions as applicable; delegate signing authority for banks, leases, and regulatory filings.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (as per pro-forma text)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Ratify and re-issue defective resolutions by unanimous written consent; retroactive authorization may be confirmed in the partnership records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax and workplace registration (Revenu Québec, CRA, CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (OneStop); Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, register the partnership with Revenu Québec for QST, source deductions, and employer contributions if applicable; register with CNESST for mandatory occupational health and safety coverage as soon as the partnership hires staff; obtain a federal business number (BN) with GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts via CRA BRO. For the low-risk cloud software scope, no financial services license is required.
required_dossiers: Identification of officers and beneficial owners
Employer information (for CNESST and CRA accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify account attributes online; contest notices under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c A-6.002) or the Excise Tax Act; voluntary GST/HST registration is retroactive for 30 days and can be aligned with the opening invoice date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking, payment rails, and PCI-DSS readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or credit union; Payments Canada (PAD rules); PCI Security Standards Council
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Canadian business bank account in the name of the Quebec limited partnership using the NEQ and governing documents; execute the pre-authorized debit (PAD) agreement for Direct Debit collection; configure Stripe Billing for subscription invoicing in CAD/USD, ensuring PCI-DSS-compliant storage of card data and adherence to PIPEDA for customer data (implementation completed in Stage 3/4).
required_dossiers: Corporate general partner resolution and incumbency
Directors' and officers' identification with proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit a corrected banking package; escalate to the bank's client remedies process; if rejected for documentation gaps, obtain certified translations from a Quebec notary and approach an alternate Schedule I bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 vertical ERP and CRM cloud software is not a licensed sector in Quebec; the contact point for investment and innovation support is the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie du Québec (MEIE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None by statute. The declaration of registration and the NEQ constitute the sole operating authorization; a municipal occupancy permit (permis d'occupation) may be required by the local city for the leased office premises, but not for the software activity itself.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based software development and cloud operations are not listed in the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment and review of certain projects (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23.1); no environmental authorization or attestation is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge thresholds apply. Leased offices must respect municipal sewer by-laws for sanitary wastewater; heating and ventilation systems must comply with the applicable building code; electronic waste generated by resold or returned hardware must be handled under the WEEE regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 37.1).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required for the office occupancy class (C/D per Quebec Fire Safety Code), including evacuation plan and extinguisher inspection; electrical and structural compliance per the Quebec Building Code; CNESST workplace registration and hazard prevention program for employees; no civil defense clearance applies to intangible cloud software services.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – federal income tax and GST/HST administration, via Business Registration Online (BRO) and the My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Québec – Quebec Sales Tax (QST), source deductions, and other provincial levies, via the CLIC portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Step 2: Apply to CRA via Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) using BRO to obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) and open a GST/HST account; non-resident partners must also obtain an Individual Tax Number using Form T1151. Step 3: Register with Revenu Québec on CLIC to open a QST account and, if employees are engaged, a source deductions and employer contributions account. Step 4: File partnership information on prescribed forms, including each partner's name, address, TIN/SIN/BN/ITN, and agreed income or loss allocation percentage. Step 5: The partnership itself holds the BN and QST account while remaining fiscally transparent; each partner reports its allocable share of Canadian-source income, and non-resident partners may be subject to 25% Part XIII withholding on deemed distributions unless an election under ITA section 216(1) is filed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; Territorial_Scope (the limited partnership is a non-taxable flow-through vehicle under section 96 of the Income Tax Act; Canadian-source business income is allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level; non-resident limited partners are subject to Canadian tax only on Canadian-source income and may face Part XIII withholding on deemed distributions).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Canadian federal law. Relevant statutory elections and classifications include: (1) the ITA section 102(2) election to cause the partnership to be a 'Canadian partnership', which limits withholding and branch tax exposure for non-resident partners; (2) the ITA section 216(1) election by a non-resident partner to file a Canadian net-basis return instead of being subject to flat withholding; (3) the ITA section 216(4) election dealing with a non-resident partner's share of Canadian business income; and (4) hybrid mismatch denial rules under ITA sections 18.2 and 18.3 (Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses) and the MLI Principal Purpose Test, which restrict favourable treatment where an entity is fiscally transparent in one jurisdiction but opaque in another.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax at 5%) and QST (Quebec value-added tax at 9.975%, computed on the GST-included price); nominal combined headline rate 14.975%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of annual worldwide taxable supplies (trailing four-quarter small-supplier threshold) for both GST/HST and QST; zero-rated export supplies count toward the threshold but no tax is collectible; a non-resident supplier whose only Canadian supplies are zero-rated exports is generally not required to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory API filing, or digital stamping regime exists in Canada or Quebec. E-invoicing is voluntary and is implemented through the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing framework based on PEPPOL BIS 3.0 via certified access points. CRA accepts electronic records and invoices provided they contain the prescribed GST/HST particulars (e.g., supplier name/BN, recipient, date, description, tax amounts) and remain legible and retrievable; Revenu Québec requires that invoices be issued in French, or bilingually, to comply with the Charter of the French Language.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of vertical cloud ERP/CRM software subscription services to non-resident customers are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, which zero-rates a supply of a service or intangible personal property made to a non-resident person where the supply is not in respect of real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or personal services supplied to an individual in Canada. The supplier must demonstrate that the customer is a non-resident and that the digital service is received and used outside Canada; similar zero-rating principles apply to the QST under the Quebec Sales Tax Act. The vendor must retain contemporaneous documentary evidence of the customer's non-resident status and of the place of digital consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed cloud SaaS/CRM subscription or master services agreement stating the customer's non-resident status, country of consumption, and delivery mechanism
Commercial invoice in a prescribed GST/HST/QST format, expressly marked as zero-rated export supply
Non-resident evidence (e.g., W-8BEN-E, certificate of residence, foreign corporate registry extract, or foreign billing address)
Inward remittance evidence (e.g., SWIFT MT103, bank credit advice, or card acquirer settlement showing funds originating from a foreign bank account)
Service delivery and access logs (e.g., IP geolocation records, server access logs, and tenant data location evidencing active receipt outside Canada)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canadian tax law does not impose a statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure represents the customary commercial and CRA audit benchmark for demonstrating the bona fide offshore collection of export proceeds. If CRA or Revenu Québec determines that the zero-rating evidence is deficient or false, the supplier is retroactively reassessed for GST at 5% and QST at 9.975%, with interest. Penalties include the Excise Tax Act section 285(1) penalty of 25% on false statements or omissions, the section 285.1 gross-negligence penalty equal to 50% of the net tax understated, and section 280 interest at prescribed rates. The normal four-year reassessment period is unlimited where misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default, and fraudulent export-credit claims may give rise to Criminal Code tax-fraud prosecution, director and partner liability, and disqualification from GST/HST registration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with supplementary regulation from the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and anti-money laundering oversight by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no exchange controls or prior approvals for inward or outward capital transfers, profit remittances, or partnership distributions. Non-resident partners can freely receive CAD or foreign-currency distributions, subject only to Quebec withholding tax obligations (governed by the Taxation Act) and FINTRAC reporting for transactions exceeding CAD 10,000. No material remittance hurdles exist; however, Quebec requires the partnership to report payments to non-residents via prescribed forms and to obtain a Relevé 24 style certificate if tax is withheld.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation deadlines for export receipts (including software licensing proceeds under ISIC 6201). Exporters may hold foreign currency in designated-currency or export accounts at any Canadian Schedule I bank. FINTRAC rules only require record keeping and reporting for single transactions of CAD 10,000 or more, and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) may require commercial invoice declarations for services rendered abroad for customs statistics.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium with specific constraints. Foreign fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, or Airwallex) can be used as settlement agents for cross-border disbursements, but they are not licensed as banks under the Bank Act and cannot provide direct membership in Payments Canada. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), payment service providers must register with the Bank of Canada before offering services to Canadian residents. A foreign EMI without a Canadian MSB license (FINTRAC) and RPAA registration cannot serve as the primary treasury rail for the Quebec LP. It is viable exclusively as a supplemental rail for low-value, recurring payments via embedded APIs, subject to an AML audit and contractual data-residency clauses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian Schedule I banks, and specifically Quebec-based institutions, require at least one authorized signatory—normally a director of the General Partner of the LP—to attend a live interview. The interview may be conducted remotely via video conference for accounts with a funded capital impairment threshold below CAD 1 million; however, in-person attendance at a Montreal or Quebec City branch is still the default for non-resident partners of a Limited Partnership. Fully remote opening is permitted when the account is introduced by a regulated Quebec corporate-services or law firm with a confirmed business address, and the registration documents are notarized and apostilled (if foreign). The bank will also require a certificate of the LP under the Québec Companies Act, showing the general partner's domicile and power to bind the partnership. Presence in person reduces the onboarding timeline from twenty business days to five business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners registered in a jurisdiction not mutually recognized by FINTRAC (e.g., a tax-haven entity without economic substance).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid memorandum of Understanding on tax information exchange (TIEA) between Canada and the partner jurisdiction; current certificate of residency for all general partners; detailed ownership chain chart with source-of-wealth narrative for each ultimate beneficial owner; and a copy of the LP's Quebec registre d'entreprises extract listing the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The LP's stated principal business is 'vertical cloud software' but revenue projections are composed of intra-group licensing royalties with no third-party customers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master subscription agreements with end customers in Canada or the US; a minimum of three qualifying software reseller contracts showing the scope of ISIC 6201 activity; SaaS platform logs showing active tenant usage; and a declaration of the virtual presence from the ISO-certified service provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A sudden injection of capital into the escrow account shortly before the first outbound vendor payment, without documented contribution history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized subscription agreements in accordance with the Quebec Partnership Act; bank statements from the contributing partner's home jurisdiction showing the source of funds; a board resolution of the general partner authorizing the specific contribution; and a completed statutory declaration for the Canada Revenue Agency under the Income Tax Act, form T2006 if the contribution exceeds CAD 100,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident partners shall be routed via SWIFT MT103 wires. The payment instruction must include a purpose code conforming to Canada's Balance of Payments / Financial Monitoring framework—use code 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital (PURPOSE: CAPINV)' for Statistics Canada reporting. A document package must accompany the wire: (a) executed capital commitment certificate; (b) LP subscription agreement; (c) a legal opinion from a Canadian securities lawyer affirming compliance with Regulation 45-106; and (d) evidence of source of funds. For contributions exceeding CAD 5 million, the transaction is reportable to Statistics Canada under the Canada Investment Act, and a Certificate of Compliance with the Quebec Partnership Act must be provided. The bank will perform a beneficial-ownership check on all partners under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Transactions must be settled in CAD at the Bank of Canada daily reference rate; the receiving bank must use a funding account with the Bank of Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the Real-Time Rail if the value is under CAD 1 million. For transfers in a foreign currency, the LP must open a designated-currency account and use the registered bank's FX desk for conversion before the intraday cut-off.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Standard vendor payments for licensing, cloud infrastructure, and professional services are settled through SWIFT MT103 (single beneficiary) for amounts up to CAD 250,000. For strategic outsourcing contracts exceeding CAD 250,000, the bank will issue an Irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) under UCP600 terms, with the beneficiary bank in the target jurisdiction. Within Canada, domestic vendor payments use the Real-Time Rail (RTR) or the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS). For subscription refunds and CRM-vertical micro-transactions under CAD 100, the LP may use Stripe's Canadian direct-debit rail (Pre-authorized Debit) subject to the Payments Canada rulebook. FX conversion for all outbound disbursements must be pre-approved by the treasurer using a standard execution policy: allocate 70% of projected requirements to spot contracts via the account bank, and 30% to one-month or three-month FX forwards.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (up to 12 months) with a Canadian Schedule I bank counterparty.
FX swaps (swap point trades) in CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/GBP for working-capital funding.
Currency options (European style, calls and puts on CAD) with mandatory premium and collateral documentation under ISDA 2002.
Cross-currency swaps (plain-vanilla fixed-for-floating) for term-debt obligations, subject to OSFI/CSA margin rules.

NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) only for thinly-traded counterparties when the bank does not have a deliverable offshore branch; CAD itself is a deliverable currency, but NDFs may be used for settlement timing around foreign exchange control windows in the counterparty's jurisdiction, not for internal hedging.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Updating Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) for registered enterprise under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ / Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 days following the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; must include general partner and partner-beneficial-ownership updates.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late notice fee of CAD 87, administrative penalties of up to CAD 5,000 for false or non-filed declarations, and after notice and publication the Registraire may cancel the registration (administrative strike-off) after continued default; once cancelled, the limited partnership loses capacity to enforce contracts in Quebec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) with Statement of Partnership Income and partner allocation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually within 5 months after the limited partnership's fiscal year-end (for December 31 year-end: due May 31; extension only for members' reporting).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Income Tax Act s.162 failure to file penalties include a minimum CAD 100 per month per return; incomplete or false returns expose partners to additional penalties under ITA s.163 and gross-negligence amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Income Return (TP-600) and Partner Relevés (Relevé 15/16/17) for the limited partnership's fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal-period end plus 6 months; for a December 31 fiscal period the return must be filed by June 30, with partner-level amounts reported on the same annual cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Revenu Québec imposes a 5% late-filing penalty on tax payable (plus 1% per full month up to 12%); an unannounced delinquency may lead to an ex officio assessment based on deemed partnership income and interest and penalty pyramiding.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit is imposed on Quebec limited partnerships solely by entity type. An independent audit is compulsory if any of the following apply: (1) the LP qualifies as a 'large partnership' under Income Tax Act subsection 248(1), generally when the cost amount of its capital property exceeds CAD 50 million; (2) the partnership agreement or un-entitled third-party creditor reports require audited financial statements; (3) the general partner or limited partners pass a consent resolution requiring audit; or (4) Revenu Québec or another securities/counterpart regulator prescribes an audited financial package.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: If financial statements are prepared, they must be in accordance with either IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), both issued by CPA Canada and adopted for Quebec partnership accounting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's enterprise legal publicity regime requires the limited partnership to identify all general partners and any limited partners having, or able to obtain, control, voting rights or a direct economic participation of 25% or more; these details are declared at registration and each year in the annual updating declaration, with changes to be declared within 30 days. This annual declaration forms the mandatory UBO confirmation protocol for a CA-LP operating in Quebec.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 350 - CAD 900 (approx. USD 260 - USD 660) per year for registered head office, legal process agent and preservation of the Quebec enterprise register record; regional mid-market TP-600/T5013 accounting and compliance package excluded.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 12,000 - CAD 35,000 (approx. USD 9,000 - USD 26,500) per audit for a revenue-stage vertical industrial ERP/CRM cloud limited partnership, excluding tax advisory.

stage_6.entry_description: Non-resident partner share of Canadian-source business income
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report allocated share; CRA T5013 issued to each partner; non-resident files Part I net-basis return (T2/T1) and obtains treaty relief where applicable.
